blocks.title: Application Security, Sandboxing, and Monitoring comparison
Application Security, Sandboxing, and Monitoring exam shortcuts
items: Example: Reject unexpected characters in a numeric field.
Protect session cookie from script access → HTTPONLY
Secure cookie attributes reduce session theft risk.
Example: HttpOnly prevents JavaScript from reading the cookie.
Find vulnerabilities without running application → STATIC CODE ANALYSIS
SAST inspects source or compiled code without execution.
Example: A scanner finds unsafe functions during CI.
Need proof software is authentic and unchanged → CODE SIGNING
Digital signatures verify publisher and integrity.
Example: An operating system verifies a signed update.
Need to execute suspicious code safely → SANDBOX
Restrict its access to the host environment.
Example: An unknown attachment opens inside a sandbox.
Need ongoing visibility after deployment → MONITORING
Collect logs and alerts to detect abnormal behavior.
Example: SIEM alerts on repeated application failures.
blocks.example: Focus on what the resource needs: baseline consistency, hardening, secure access, isolation, authentication, or monitoring.

questions.q: A web application rejects unexpected characters and enforces strict formats before processing user input. Which control is this?
questions.explanation: Input validation checks and sanitizes external input before processing.

questions.q: A session cookie should not be readable by client-side JavaScript. Which setting is most relevant?
questions.explanation: HttpOnly prevents client-side JavaScript from reading the cookie.

questions.q: A development team wants to detect vulnerabilities by scanning source code without executing the application. Which technique is this?
questions.explanation: Static code analysis examines code without running the application.

questions.q: An operating system verifies that a software update came from the expected publisher and was not modified. Which control is this?
questions.explanation: Code signing verifies publisher identity and code integrity.

questions.q: An unknown attachment should be executed in a restricted environment so it cannot freely access the host. Which technique is best?
questions.explanation: Sandboxing isolates untrusted code from the host environment.

questions.q: A SIEM alerts when an application begins generating abnormal authentication failures. Which control is being used?
questions.explanation: Monitoring observes telemetry and generates alerts on suspicious behavior.
